summary: The municipal Lanna Folklife Centre presents Lanna ways of life through twelve permanent exhibit areas, including ritual objects, Buddhist art, murals, textiles, ceramics, music and the history of the former courthouse building. It is an approachable, indoor introduction to the culture and craft behind Chiang Mai's temples and neighbourhoods, in the Three Kings precinct.
whyGo: See a broad range of Lanna material culture and religious art in one compact visit.
Connect the city's temple architecture, textiles and customs with objects and explanations indoors.

The museum's current temporary show, 'The Beloved Box of Memory', focuses on Lanna household craft and keepsakes; its official listing says it has been on display since 17 January 2026, with no end date shown.
bestFor: First-time visitors looking for cultural context before exploring Chiang Mai's temples
People interested in local craft, Buddhist art, textiles and everyday objects
A rainy or hot part of a day in the Old City
skipIf: Monday or Tuesday is your only available day; the current schedule lists the museum as closed.
You need confirmed step-free access throughout; the official material reviewed does not describe access facilities.
You are seeking a large collection of original artefacts or contemporary art rather than an interpretive overview.
duration: Planning estimate: allow 60–90 minutes for the permanent displays and any temporary exhibition; reading every panel may take longer.
cost: The municipal site currently lists ฿90 per adult and ฿40 per child. Recheck before December 2026, as prices can change; transport and any other museums are extra.
hours: The municipal site currently lists 08:30–16:30, Wednesday–Sunday, including public holidays; closed Monday and Tuesday. Confirm year-end exceptions before setting out.
bestTime: Visit near opening for a quieter start, or use the museum as a midday indoor break. If visiting the nearby heritage cluster, start here before walking to other sights while it is still cool.
gettingThere: At Prapokklao Road in the Si Phum area of the Old City, near Three Kings Monument. Walk if staying centrally; otherwise use a tuk-tuk or taxi and give the driver 'Lanna Folklife Centre' or Three Kings Monument as the destination. The official museum page has a directions link and phone number.
booking: The official page lists admission and a contact number but no advance-booking requirement for ordinary visits. Call +66 53 217 793 to confirm opening, group arrangements or holiday hours.
accessibility: The official pages reviewed do not specify step-free routes, lifts, accessible toilets or other access provisions. Contact the museum ahead of time if access is important and ask which galleries can be reached without stairs.
practicalTips: Check the municipal museum page again close to your visit; hours and admission here are current listings, not a December 2026 guarantee.
The permanent display includes twelve areas; choose a few themes of interest if you have limited time.
Combine with the nearby Three Kings Monument and other central museums, checking each one's separate opening days.
decemberNotes: This is a useful indoor stop during Chiang Mai's popular cool-season travel period. As checked on 17 October 2026, the official page listed the long-running 'The Beloved Box of Memory' exhibition as on display from January 2026 onward but gave no closing date. No December 2026-specific event or closure notice was verified; the museum's general listing says it opens on public holidays, but confirm around year-end.
uncertainties: The official site gives no end date for 'The Beloved Box of Memory', so its presence in December 2026 is not guaranteed.
December 2026 holiday hours and any special programming were not published in the material reviewed.
Accessibility details are not documented in the official sources reviewed.
Admission and weekly hours may change before the trip.
